question: Requirements for upgrading to MySQL version 8

answers:
Before upgrading to MySQL version 8, you should follow these requirements:
1. Check for an upgrade with Upgrade Checker Utility in MySQL Shell to check if an upgrade is required for MySQL.
2. Before attempting any upgrades, refer to MySQL's Preparing Your Installation for Upgrade. to ensure upgrade readiness.
3. Change the authentication plugin: In MySQL 8.0, caching_sha2_password is the default authentication plugin rather than mysql_native_password. If you encounter the error 'sha256_password is deprecated and will be removed in a future release', you need to ALTER affected Users to use 'caching_sha2_password'.
For more information about the upgrade process, you can refer to the IBM Cloud Databases documentation on migrating to Databases for MySQL.

history.content: How can one upgrade to a new version using the IBM Cloud CLI and restore from backup?

To upgrade to a new version and restore from backup using the IBM Cloud CLI,  clicking Restore on a backup brings up a dialog box where you can change some options for the new deployment. One of them is the database version, which is auto-populated with the versions available for you to upgrade to. Select a version and click Restore to start the provision and restore process.  Here's an example for upgrading and restoring a MySQL database:
```bash
ibmcloud resource service-instance-create example-upgrade databases-for-mysql standard us-south -p '{"backup_id": "crn:v1:bluemix:public:databases-for-mysql:us-south:a/54e8ffe85dcedf470db5b5ee6ac4a8d8:1b8f53db-fc2d-4e24-8470-f82b15c71717:backup:06392e97-df90-46d8-98e8-cb67e9e0a8e6", "version":8}'

For more information, see [SHA-256 Pluggable Authentication](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sha256-pluggable-authentication.html).







 Back up and Restore Upgrade 

To upgrade your database, initiate the process by [restoring a backup](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mysql?topic=databases-for-mysql-dashboard-backups&interface=clirestore-backup-cli) of your data into a new deployment that is running the new database version.



 Upgrading in the UI 

You can upgrade to a new version when [restoring a backup](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mysql?topic=databases-for-mysql-dashboard-backups&interface=clirestore-backup-cli) from the Backups menu of your Deployment dashboard. Clicking Restore on a backup brings up a dialog box where you can change some options for the new deployment.

1.  Create and export a v5.7x backup.
2.  Migrate and prepare your backup locally to be compatible with 8.0.
3.  Import into ICD MySQL 8.0.



As a best practice, retain your current v5.7 backups until the version 8 import is evaluated. Use mysqldump or mydumper to export your 5.7.x databases. For more information, see [Migrating to Databases for MySQL](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mysql?topic=databases-for-mysql-migrating).

Once your upgrade is complete, changes cannot be reverted. The changes are incompatible, and you cannot use the data directory from MySQL 8.0 on MySQL 5.7. Retain your MySQL v5.7 backup, as it helps to restore it on a MySQL 5.7 instance should the changes need to be reversed.



  Upgrade Prerequisites 

Before attempting any upgrades, refer to MySQL's [Preparing Your Installation for Upgrade](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/upgrade-prerequisites.html) to ensure upgrade readiness.

* CLI
* API







 Upgrading to a new Major Version 

Once a major version of a database is at its End Of Life (EOL), upgrade to a current major version.

Find the available versions of MySQL on the [IBM Cloud® Databases for MySQL catalog](https://cloud.ibm.com/databases/databases-for-mysql/create) page, from the Cloud Databases CLI plug-in command [ibmcloud cdb deployables-show](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-cli-plugin?topic=databases-cli-plugin-cdb-referencedeployables-show), or from the Cloud Databases API [/deployables](https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/cloud-databases-apiget-all-deployable-databases) endpoint.
